sections.h2: Where do Berrien County property owners deal with tax?
sections.html:
Nashville is the county seat, and the Tax Commissioner works from the first floor of the Administration Building at 201 N. Davis Street, Suite 105, Nashville, Georgia 31639. Phone (229) 686-7461 for billing and payment questions, with the office open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The commissioner bills and collects real property, personal property, mobile home, motor vehicle and timber tax.

Valuation is a different office. Berrien's Board of Tax Assessors sets values and takes homestead applications, and the Tax Commissioner's staff can point you to the assessors if you are unsure where to go.

  • Tax Commissioner: bills, receipts, payment help, liens.
  • Tax Assessor: values, returns, homestead and other exemptions.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: warranty deed copies at the courthouse deed room.

sections.h2: What shapes a house sale in Berrien County?
sections.html:
Berrien lies in south central Georgia, and the General Assembly created it on February 25, 1856 from parts of Coffee, Irwin and Lowndes counties. It spans 458 square miles, most of it rural, with the western side draining toward the Withlacoochee River and the eastern side toward the Alapaha. Irwin, Coffee, Atkinson, Lanier, Lowndes, Cook and Tift counties touch its borders. A single school system, the Berrien County School District, serves every resident.

The county lost an unusually high share of its young men in World War I, and a copper Doughboy memorial by E. M. Viquesney stands on the Nashville courthouse grounds. Population has bounced around: 19,286 in 2010, 18,160 in 2020 and a 2025 estimate of 18,932, which is 4.3 percent above the 2020 base. About 73 percent of residents lived outside urban areas at the 2020 count, so most owners here live on rural parcels rather than in town.

sections.h2: When must Berrien County property tax be paid?
sections.html:
The county's tax office states that real estate and business personal property taxes have been due every November 15 since 2018. Mobile and manufactured homes are due on April 1. Motor vehicle tax is tied to the owner's birthday.

The cost of paying late is spelled out on the same FAQ. Interest is 1 percent a month after the due date, and a 10 percent penalty attaches to anything not paid within 90 days of the deadline. Unpaid tax can also be recorded as a FiFa lien with the Clerk of Superior Court, which the FAQ says may happen once taxes sit more than 30 days past due, and the tax commissioner can levy on property when a bill stays unpaid.

sections.h2: How does Berrien County calculate a tax bill?
sections.html:
Georgia taxes 40 percent of fair market value, and the Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education each set a millage rate every year. Berrien's tax office explains the order: subtract exemptions from the assessed figure to get net taxable value, then multiply by the mills. One mill equals a dollar for every $1,000 of that taxable value.

Ask the commissioner for the millage on your parcel instead of guessing at it. Statements are mailed to the owner and not to a mortgage company. If a lender escrows for you, make sure the servicer has the Berrien bill.

  • Returns: any owner may declare a value between January 1 and April 1.
  • Notice: the assessors mail a notice only when they disagree with the return.
  • Bill: the commissioner multiplies the net taxable value by the adopted mills.

sections.h2: How do I get homestead exemption in Berrien County?
sections.html:
Own the home and live in it on January 1, then apply at the tax assessor's office so the application is received before April 1. Applications can be turned in all year, but one that arrives after April 1 takes effect the next year.

Once approved, the exemption stays in place if you remain in the same house. Move to another Berrien address and you must file again. Owners who reach age 62 can ask about an added exemption, and business personal property may qualify for the freeport exemption. Ask the assessors for the current dollar amounts, because they can differ by county and change with legislation.

sections.h2: What can I do if I disagree with a Berrien County value?
sections.html:
Appeal within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. The appeal goes to the Berrien County Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator, and if the result is unsatisfactory you can continue to superior court by giving the Board of Tax Assessors a written notice.

The Georgia Department of Revenue adds that an appeal about fair market value should be postmarked by the 45th day and sent to the assessors. Money paid on tax that was erroneously or illegally charged can be recovered if you ask in writing within three years of payment.

sections.h2: What should I do about taxes if I plan to sell my Berrien County house?
sections.html:
Get the tax balance in writing from the commissioner before you accept an offer, and confirm who is billed. The county lists the owner on January 1, so a statement can arrive in your name after a late-year sale. Whoever handles your closing can show how the year's tax is split.

A FiFa recorded for unpaid tax is a public record, and it has to be paid off before a buyer can receive clean title. Houses in rural Berrien with old taxes, inherited deeds or needed repairs are still sellable as is, because the payoff comes out of the sale money. A cash buyer will want the same payoff figure you have.

faqs.q: What is the due date for Berrien County property tax?
faqs.a: November 15 each year for real estate and business personal property, a schedule the county has used since 2018. Mobile homes are due April 1.

faqs.q: What penalty does Berrien County add to late property tax?
faqs.a: Interest of 1 percent per month starts after the due date, and a 10 percent penalty applies if the tax is not paid within 90 days of the deadline.

faqs.q: Where is the Berrien County tax office?
faqs.a: It is on the first floor of the Administration Building at 201 N. Davis Street, Suite 105, in Nashville, and the phone is (229) 686-7461. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

faqs.q: How soon must I appeal a Berrien County assessment?
faqs.a: Within 45 days of the date of the assessment notice. Send the appeal to the Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator.

faqs.q: Does the Berrien tax bill go to my lender?
faqs.a: No, the Tax Commissioner mails statements to the homeowner and never to the mortgage company. If your lender escrows, forward the bill or confirm that the servicer pays it.
